purpose: How an operator of a payroll referral or service practice chooses which engagement rung to stand on (introduce-only referral partner, wholesale reseller who owns the invoice, or service bureau doing the work inside a platform's accountant console), verifies how the partner program actually pays and credits them, builds the advisor channels that produce payroll clients, profiles a prospect's payroll complexity well enough to recommend or decline honestly, and times the switch against the year and quarter boundaries that govern when a small business can realistically change payroll providers.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is not a licensed tax preparer, attorney, or enrolled practitioner acting in that capacity here; everything in this knowledge base is commercial and operational judgement, not tax or legal advice
the payroll platform and its partner program are third parties whose published terms, capabilities, and compensation structures change without notice and must be re-read per deal rather than recalled

the client, not the referrer, is generally the party legally responsible for its employment tax obligations; who may act as an agent for filing or deposit is a jurisdiction-specific and platform-specific question to verify, never to assume

prospects are small employers whose payroll data contains government identifiers, wage detail, and bank account information, so every acquisition-stage practice is designed around collecting the least data that answers the question

compensation amounts, platform pricing, and client counts are treated as mechanisms and qualitative bands because no verified figures were supplied; any specific number must be read from the current partner agreement or platform price sheet at the time of the deal
exclusions: the onboarding project itself: entity and tax-account setup execution, employee data migration, year-to-date balance loading, direct-deposit setup, parallel-run verification and cutover, and the operational service-boundary matrix between platform, service layer and client, all of which belong to the sibling onboarding knowledge base

the recurring service rhythm after go-live: per-run pre-flight and post-run checks, quarter-end and year-end filing calendars as operating mechanisms, issue triage between client and platform, retention through error-free runs, and expansion into bookkeeping, HR or benefits add-ons, all of which belong to the sibling recurring-relationship knowledge base
tax advice of any kind, including how a specific wage, benefit, or fringe item should be taxed, whether a particular deposit schedule applies, or how to respond to a specific agency notice

legal advice, including whether a specific worker is an employee or a contractor, whether a particular referral fee arrangement is permissible for a particular licensee, and the drafting of enforceable contracts

asserting specific commission rates, revenue-share percentages, platform prices, per-employee fees, clawback windows, or client-count tiers as fact; this knowledge base teaches the mechanism that produces such a number and the verification step that reads the current one

asserting jurisdiction-specific registration requirements, filing deadlines, form identifiers, or penalty amounts as fact; obligation classes are named and the operator is directed to verify current rules in the relevant jurisdiction
performing payroll runs, filings, deposits, or amendments as the professional of record, and holding the client's agency credentials on their behalf
any selling practice that manufactures fear, exploits an overwhelmed or distressed operator, or conceals how the operator is compensated

competency_questions.question: Which engagement rung should this operator stand on - introduce-only referral partner, wholesale reseller who owns the invoice, or service bureau running payroll inside the platform - given their capability, liability appetite, capital, and how they want to be paid?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGAGEMENT_MODEL_LADDER states the three rungs and the capability, liability and cash-timing tests that select one, and REFERRAL_PARTNER_RUNG, RESELLER_WHOLESALE_RUNG and SERVICE_BUREAU_RUNG each state what the operator owns and answers for on that rung

competency_questions.question: Where is the line between explaining how payroll and employment tax mechanics work and giving tax or legal advice, and what does the operator say when a prospect walks them over that line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROFESSIONAL_SCOPE_LIMITS distinguishes mechanism explanation from advice, names the referral-out response, and states that the client remains the responsible party for its own tax obligations regardless of who presses the button

competency_questions.question: How does the money actually arrive on each rung, what moves its size, and how is the current number verified for a specific deal rather than assumed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVENUE_SHARE_MECHANICS names the payment forms (one-time bounty, ongoing share of platform subscription, wholesale spread, own service fee), the drivers that move each, and the per-deal verification step against the current partner agreement

competency_questions.question: How does a referral actually get credited to this operator, what makes credit silently fail, and what exposure exists if a client leaves early?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ATTRIBUTION_AND_CLAWBACK_LEDGER describes the credit mechanisms, the common attribution failure paths, the clawback exposure class, and the operator-side ledger that makes a dispute winnable

competency_questions.question: How should the payroll platform and its partner program be evaluated before the operator stakes client relationships and referral-source credibility on it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLATFORM_PROGRAM_DILIGENCE lists the evidence classes to gather (tax filing service model, error and penalty handling posture, support reachability, partner console capability, program change history, concentration exposure) and the disqualifying findings

competency_questions.question: What must be learned about a prospect's payroll before anyone can say whether it is a fit, and how is that learned without collecting sensitive employee data too early?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_COMPLEXITY_PROFILE enumerates the profile dimensions that drive fit and effort, and CLIENT_DATA_MINIMIZATION states the aggregate-first collection rule and what must never be requested at the acquisition stage

competency_questions.question: Which classes of employer registration and tax-account obligation make a payroll deal complex, and how are they raised with a prospect without asserting jurisdiction specifics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_REGISTRATION_CLASSES names the obligation classes (federal employer identification, state or provincial withholding accounts, unemployment insurance accounts, local or municipal taxes where they exist, agency power-of-attorney or third-party access classes) and attaches the verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction instruction to each

competency_questions.question: When should the operator tell a prospect that this platform is the wrong answer, and how is that done without destroying the relationship or the referral source's trust?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_PLATFORM_MATCH states the capability tests that trigger a decline, the recommend-elsewhere script, and the rule that a compensation difference may never decide a fit question

competency_questions.question: Which referral sources actually produce payroll clients, what does each one want in return, and how is a channel worked so it keeps producing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERRAL_CHANNEL_PORTFOLIO maps the source classes with the motive and lead quality of each, and BOOKKEEPER_CPA_ALLIANCE explains the deepest vein, its reciprocity structure, and the do-not-poach covenant that keeps it open

competency_questions.question: What must be agreed in writing with a referral source, and what restrictions might prevent a particular source from accepting a share at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARTNER_FEE_SHARING_HYGIENE lists the terms a written arrangement must fix and names the restriction classes (professional-body independence and commission rules, insurance producer compensation rules, employer and platform policies) with the verify-before-promising instruction

competency_questions.question: What actually makes a small employer change payroll providers, and how are those triggers found rather than manufactured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SWITCHING_TRIGGER_MAP enumerates the real trigger classes and their observable signals, and PENALTY_TALK_DISCIPLINE states how compliance risk is discussed without fear-selling

competency_questions.question: How do the year-end and quarter-end boundaries shape the pipeline, and when is breaking the calendar to switch mid-cycle the right advice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOUNDARY_TIMING_CALENDAR explains why a boundary cutover is cheaper, what a mid-cycle switch adds in work and risk, the lead-time consequence for pipeline building, and the specific conditions that justify not waiting

competency_questions.question: How is a discovery conversation run so it surfaces the real cost and risk of the prospect's current arrangement without pressuring an overwhelmed owner?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAIN_DISCOVERY_INTERVIEW gives the question sequence and the evidence it seeks, and PENALTY_TALK_DISCIPLINE gives the vulnerable-operator care rules and the prohibited framings

competency_questions.question: What exactly is being sold, how is the price built from the operator's own economics, and what must be true before a won deal is handed to onboarding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFFER_SCOPE_AND_PRICE_FRAME separates platform subscription from the operator's service layer and builds price from touch-time and complexity rather than a copied figure, and WON_DEAL_HANDOFF_PACKET states the contents and pass conditions of the packet that leaves acquisition

glossary.definition: An arrangement in which the operator introduces a prospect to a payroll platform and the platform owns the sale, the contract, the billing, the service and the liability; the operator is compensated by the platform for the introduction and has no service obligation to the client.

An arrangement in which the operator buys platform capacity at a partner rate, bills the client directly at a price the operator sets, and therefore owns the invoice, the receivable, the first line of support and the commercial relationship, with the spread between wholesale and retail as the revenue mechanism.

A practice in which the operator does the recurring payroll work for the client inside the platform's accountant or partner console - entering or reviewing hours, running the payroll, watching the filing calendar - and charges a service fee for that labour, which may sit alongside a platform revenue share.

Any ongoing partner compensation expressed as a portion of what the client pays the platform, as distinct from a one-time introduction bounty; its size, duration and survival conditions are set by the current partner agreement and must be read there, never assumed.

The period after a client starts during which the platform may reverse or withhold partner compensation if the client cancels, fails to pay, or is found to have been credited in error; the existence, length and trigger conditions of such a window are program-specific terms to verify before relying on the income.

The mechanism by which a platform decides that a given signed client belongs to a given partner - a tracked link, a partner code entered at signup, a submitted lead form, or a rep-logged introduction - and the point at which most partner income is silently lost when the mechanism is bypassed.

The cumulative wage, tax, deduction and employer-contribution totals already recorded for each employee in the current tax year, which must be carried across when a client changes provider mid-year; their existence is the reason a boundary cutover is cheaper than a mid-cycle one, though the migration work itself belongs to onboarding.

A concrete event in the prospect's world that converts payroll dissatisfaction into action - an agency notice, a botched or late filing, a price increase, the loss of the person who used to do it, a first hire in a new jurisdiction, an acquisition, or a year-end that forces a decision anyway.

The categories of registration an employer generally needs before payroll can be filed on its behalf - a federal or national employer identifier, a jurisdiction-level income tax withholding account, an unemployment or social insurance account, and in some places municipal or local accounts - named as classes because their names, thresholds and procedures differ by jurisdiction and must be verified there.

An insurance billing arrangement in which the workers compensation premium is calculated from each actual payroll run rather than an upfront estimate, which is the reason insurance producers have a direct commercial interest in where their clients run payroll and are therefore a live referral channel.

nodes.definition: Decide, before any prospecting, which of three structurally different businesses is being built, because each carries a different obligation set, cash-flow shape and ceiling. On the introduce-only rung the operator hands a warm prospect to the platform and is paid for the introduction; the platform owns contract, billing, service and error liability, and the operator's asset is the referral flow itself. On the wholesale reseller rung the operator buys platform capacity at a partner rate, sets and issues the client's invoice, and thereby inherits the receivable, the price objection, the first support call and a commercial expectation that someone will answer when a run goes wrong. On the service-bureau rung the operator does the recurring work inside the platform's partner console and charges for labour, which produces the highest revenue per client and the highest exposure, since a missed input on the operator's side becomes the client's filing problem. The selection test is not ambition but capability, coverage and cash: whether the operator can absorb a support call on a payday, whether they carry appropriate professional liability coverage for the rung they claim, whether they can float a wholesale bill, and whether their existing skills are relationship skills or payroll-execution skills. The rungs can be climbed over time and can coexist across segments, but claiming a rung the operator cannot staff is the single most common structural error in this business.

included: the three-rung structure and what is owned on each
the capability, liability-coverage and cash tests that select a rung
mixed-rung operation across client segments and the migration path between rungs
excluded: the operational division of duties between platform, service layer and client after go-live, which the onboarding knowledge base defines
the mechanics of the recurring per-run service, which the recurring-relationship knowledge base defines
legal advice on entity form, insurance adequacy or contract enforceability

pros.claim: Naming the rung up front makes every later question decidable, because who owns the invoice and who answers the payday phone call determines pricing, staffing and the promise made to referral sources
pros.example: an operator who has chosen introduce-only can answer a prospect's request for a discount instantly - the platform sets the price, not them - instead of improvising a concession they cannot fund

pros.claim: The ladder frames growth as a deliberate capability upgrade rather than a drift, so the operator adds obligations only when they have the staffing and coverage to carry them
pros.example: moving from introductions to a service practice only after a second trained person exists, so a single illness during a pay week does not become a client filing failure

cons.claim: The introduce-only rung concentrates almost all leverage in the platform, which can change program terms, price, or capability without the operator's consent
cons.example: a partner program restructuring its compensation form while the operator's entire pipeline was built on the previous structure

cons.claim: Choosing a rung early can misfit a market the operator has not met yet, since prospects in some segments will only buy a full service practice and others will only buy software
cons.example: an operator committed to introduce-only meeting a run of restaurant prospects who want someone to actually run payroll each week and having nothing to sell them

failure_modes: claiming service-bureau capability while staffed as an introducer, so the first payday emergency has no owner
operating on the reseller rung without confirming whether the operator may lawfully bill for the platform's service in that arrangement
letting the rung be chosen implicitly by whatever the first client demanded
assuming the platform's liability posture carries over to the rung above it
acceptance_tests: a written statement names the rung, what the operator owns on it, what the platform owns, and what the client owns, in one page a referral source could read
the chosen rung is matched to a staffing answer for the payday-emergency case and to a professional liability coverage question the operator has actually asked their insurer
revisit_triggers: the platform changes partner program structure, permitted billing arrangements, or console capability
the operator adds or loses the staff capacity that the current rung assumes
a segment of prospects repeatedly asks for a service level the current rung cannot supply

base.update_signal: the platform publishes revised partner program tiers or permitted billing arrangements, or the operator's staffing and insurance coverage change enough to make a different rung supportable

nodes.definition: Fix and rehearse the line between explaining how payroll mechanics work and advising a specific employer on its specific tax or legal position, because payroll sits inside a compliance-critical professional domain where a wrong answer produces assessed penalties and interest for the client and a credibility loss the operator cannot buy back. Mechanism explanation is safe and is the operator's actual product: how a pay run turns hours into gross, how withholding and employer contributions are calculated by the platform, which classes of account an employer generally needs before filings can be made, what a parallel run is for, why a mid-year change carries balance-migration work. Advice is the other side of the line: telling a specific employer that a specific worker may be treated as a contractor, that a specific fringe benefit is not taxable, that a specific deposit schedule applies to them, or how to answer a specific agency notice. The operating rule is to answer the class question, refuse the instance question, and hand the instance to a qualified professional in the client's jurisdiction, in writing, before the conversation moves on. Two further facts belong in the same rehearsed script: the employer generally remains the party responsible for its own employment tax obligations no matter who operates the software, and jurisdictional specifics must be verified in the client's own jurisdiction rather than recalled from another client's situation.

included: the class-versus-instance test and the rehearsed refusal-and-referral script
the statement that the employer remains the responsible party
the verify-in-jurisdiction instruction attached to every regulatory reference
excluded: any actual tax, legal, or classification determination for a named client
the operational handling of notices and agency correspondence after go-live, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base
professional licensure decisions about what credential the operator should obtain

pros.claim: A rehearsed boundary keeps the operator useful under pressure, because the answer to a question they must not answer is prepared rather than improvised in front of a client who wants reassurance
pros.example: responding to a prospect's fringe-benefit taxation question with an explanation of how the platform applies a taxability setting plus a written referral to their tax professional, rather than a guess that becomes a promise

pros.claim: Naming the employer as the responsible party early prevents the silent assumption that hiring a referral partner transfers legal responsibility, which is the assumption behind most later disputes
pros.example: stating in the first meeting that filings are made for the employer and remain the employer's obligation, so a later notice is handled as a shared investigation rather than as an accusation

cons.claim: Strict boundaries can read as evasiveness to a small employer who wanted one confident answer, and some prospects will prefer a competitor who gives them one
cons.example: losing a prospect to someone who cheerfully told them their whole crew could stay on contractor paperwork

cons.claim: Referring out repeatedly adds friction and cost for the client and can stall a deal while a third professional is scheduled
cons.example: a classification question that parks a signature for weeks while the prospect waits on their accountant

failure_modes: answering an instance question because the class answer felt obviously applicable
repeating another client's jurisdictional specifics as if they were general rules
implying that the platform or the operator absorbs the employer's tax responsibility
giving the boundary verbally but writing marketing copy that promises compliance outcomes
acceptance_tests: a written scope statement distinguishes explanation from advice with at least one worked example on each side, and appears in the operator's proposal and marketing copy without contradiction
every regulatory reference in client-facing material carries an explicit instruction to verify current rules in the client's jurisdiction with a qualified professional
revisit_triggers: the operator obtains or loses a professional credential that changes what they may do
a client asks a question the current script does not classify
marketing or proposal language is found promising a compliance outcome

base.update_signal: a regulator or professional body issues guidance on what unlicensed payroll intermediaries may represent, or the operator's own credential status changes

nodes.definition: Design the acquisition stage so that the operator can qualify, quote and recommend while holding almost none of the prospect's sensitive payroll data, because payroll data is the densest concentration of harmful information a small business holds - government identifiers, full wage histories, home addresses, bank account and routing details - and an acquisition-stage leak destroys the referral channel that produced the deal as well as the deal. The practical rule is aggregate-first: employee headcount, contractor headcount, pay frequency, jurisdictions worked in, pay types present, and benefit deduction classes answer every fit and pricing question without a single name attached. When a document is genuinely needed to verify something - a redacted payroll register summary to see which deduction classes exist, or an invoice to see what the incumbent charges - it is requested redacted, transmitted through a channel the operator controls rather than by open email, held for a stated purpose, and deleted on a stated schedule. Credential sharing is refused outright: the operator never asks for, accepts, or stores the prospect's login to their current payroll system or to a tax agency portal, and explains why in a way that raises rather than lowers trust. This node is a first-class discipline, not a policy appendix, because the cheapest moment to leak data is the enthusiastic pre-sale moment when nobody has signed anything and no controls exist yet.

included: the aggregate-first qualification data set
redaction, controlled-channel transfer, stated purpose and deletion schedule for any pre-sale document
the refusal of credential sharing and the explanation that accompanies it
excluded: post-signature data collection, migration and secure loading of employee records, which belongs to the onboarding knowledge base
the platform's own security architecture and its contractual data-processing commitments
legal advice on privacy statutes, breach notification duties, or data processing agreements

pros.claim: Holding aggregates rather than records makes an acquisition-stage incident survivable, because there is nothing sensitive in the operator's inbox to lose
pros.example: qualifying a twenty-person landscaping company from headcount, pay frequency, jurisdiction and deduction classes alone, with no employee named anywhere in the operator's files

pros.claim: Visible restraint is itself a sales asset with an audience that is being asked to trust a stranger with wages and bank details
pros.example: declining an offered spreadsheet of employee records and explaining what is actually needed instead, which a cautious owner reads as competence

cons.claim: Aggregates hide complexity that only shows up in the detail, so a fit judgement made on summary data can miss an expensive quirk
cons.example: a headcount summary that conceals a small group of employees with wage garnishments and multi-jurisdiction withholding

cons.claim: Redaction and controlled channels add friction that some prospects experience as bureaucracy from a small vendor
cons.example: an owner who wanted to just forward last month's payroll report and is now asked to redact and upload it

failure_modes: accepting an unsolicited unredacted payroll register and leaving it in an email account
asking for identifiers or bank details before there is a signed relationship that needs them
logging into the prospect's incumbent system with the prospect's own credentials to look around
keeping pre-sale documents indefinitely because the deal might come back
acceptance_tests: the qualification form collects only aggregate fields, and a review of the operator's pre-sale files finds no unredacted employee-level data
a written retention and deletion rule exists for pre-sale documents and a deletion pass has actually been run against lost or dormant deals
revisit_triggers: a prospect or referral source sends unredacted employee data unsolicited
a new intake tool, form, or storage location enters the sales process
a platform or partner program changes what it requires a partner to collect before signup

base.update_signal: a privacy or breach-notification obligation applicable to the operator changes, or an incident or near-miss reveals sensitive data sitting in an uncontrolled acquisition-stage channel

nodes.definition: State how the operator is paid before making the recommendation, not after the prospect asks and not buried in a proposal footer, because every recommendation in this business is a compensated recommendation and the prospect's ability to weigh it depends on knowing that. The disclosure is short, specific about form rather than amount, and delivered at the moment the operator first names a platform: that the operator is a partner of the platform and is compensated by it, whether that compensation is a one-time introduction payment or continues while the client stays, and whether the operator also charges the client separately for service work. The same disclosure is owed in both directions - to the client about the platform relationship, and to a referring bookkeeper or agent about what the operator will and will not do with the client they were handed. Disclosure is also a filter that improves the practice: an operator who must say aloud that they are paid ongoing for this recommendation becomes markedly less willing to recommend a platform that does not fit, which is exactly the intended effect. Where a jurisdiction, professional body, or platform program imposes a specific disclosure form or wording, that obligation class is verified and followed rather than assumed to be satisfied by informal honesty.

included: timing, content and audience of the compensation disclosure
the two-directional duty to client and to referral source
the obligation to verify whether a prescribed disclosure form applies
excluded: disclosing the specific amount of partner compensation, which is a commercial term between operator and platform
the drafting of the referral agreement itself
post-sale service communications, which belong to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Early disclosure removes the single most damaging late-stage discovery, which is a prospect learning from someone else that the recommendation was paid for
pros.example: an owner hearing from their accountant that the introducer earns ongoing compensation, after the introducer had presented the choice as neutral

pros.claim: Saying it out loud disciplines the recommendation itself, because a conflicted recommendation is much harder to make with the conflict named in the room
pros.example: an operator hesitating to push a platform onto a poor-fit prospect immediately after explaining that they are paid while that client stays

cons.claim: Some prospects discount everything said after the disclosure and revert to a self-serve comparison the operator cannot influence
cons.example: an owner who thanks the operator, takes the shortlist, and signs up directly without the partner attribution

cons.claim: Disclosure invites a discount demand, since a prospect who knows the operator is paid may ask for that value back
cons.example: a prospect asking for the introduction payment to be rebated to them, which may itself be restricted in some arrangements

failure_modes: disclosing only in writing in a document the prospect will not read
disclosing after the recommendation has already landed
describing compensation vaguely enough that the prospect believes it is a token amount
omitting the disclosure to a referral source about how their client will be handled
acceptance_tests: a one-sentence spoken disclosure exists, is used at first platform mention, and is mirrored in the written proposal
the operator has checked whether any professional body, regulator, or partner program prescribes a disclosure form for their situation, and recorded the answer
revisit_triggers: the compensation form changes from one-time to ongoing or vice versa
the operator begins charging clients directly in addition to receiving partner compensation
a prospect or referral source expresses surprise about how the operator is paid

base.update_signal: a partner program, professional body, or consumer regulator introduces a prescribed disclosure format, or the operator's compensation structure changes form

nodes.definition: Run the introduce-only rung as a lead-quality business rather than a volume business, because on this rung the operator's only lever is which prospects reach the platform and how well prepared they arrive. The mechanics are simple and the discipline is not: the operator identifies a prospect with a real switching trigger, confirms basic fit against the platform's capability, discloses the compensation relationship, hands over through whatever attribution mechanism the program requires, and then stays present as a relationship owner without pretending to control the platform's sales or service. What the operator owns is the introduction, the expectation-setting and the referral source's trust; what the operator does not own is pricing, the contract, the implementation timeline, or the recovery when a run goes wrong. The obligation that most often gets skipped is expectation management in both directions: telling the prospect honestly what the platform does and does not do, and telling the platform enough about the prospect's complexity that the sale is not made on a false picture. The economics are thin per client and depend on flow, which makes the referral channel portfolio and the attribution ledger the two nodes this rung actually stands on; without flow this rung is a hobby, and without attribution it is unpaid work.

included: what the operator owns and does not own on the introduce-only rung
the handover and expectation-setting obligations in both directions
the flow-dependence of this rung's economics
excluded: running payroll or touching the client's data after handover
the platform's own sales process, pricing and implementation
post-go-live service, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: The rung carries almost no execution liability, so an operator can build a payroll income stream alongside another practice without adding a payday obligation
pros.example: a bookkeeper who introduces payroll clients and keeps their evenings, because a failed direct deposit is the platform's incident to run

pros.claim: Low fixed cost means the rung survives a slow quarter, since the operator carries no wholesale bill and no service payroll of their own
pros.example: an operator with no closes in a quiet stretch losing time rather than cash

cons.claim: The operator inherits the platform's service quality without any control over it, and a bad implementation damages the operator's referral source relationship first
cons.example: a CPA who sent three clients and stops sending any after the second one's first run is late

cons.claim: Per-client economics are thin and entirely program-defined, so the operator's income can be restructured by a decision they do not participate in
cons.example: a program moving from ongoing share to one-time payment, changing the operator's business model overnight

failure_modes: introducing prospects the platform obviously cannot serve to keep volume up
overselling the platform's capability to make the handover easier
disappearing after the handover so the referral source hears nothing about their own client
letting the prospect sign up directly and losing attribution entirely
acceptance_tests: each introduction is recorded with its attribution mechanism, the complexity summary passed to the platform, and the date of the expectation-setting conversation
a post-handover check with both the client and the referral source occurs within the operator's stated follow-up window and is logged
revisit_triggers: platform implementation or support quality changes in a way referral sources notice
the program changes attribution or compensation mechanics
introduced clients begin failing fit at a rate that suggests the qualification step is too loose

base.update_signal: the platform publishes changed partner obligations or attribution requirements, or referral sources report a systematic change in post-handover client experience

nodes.definition: Run the wholesale rung as a small subscription business with a real balance sheet, because owning the invoice changes everything about the operation. The operator buys platform capacity at a partner rate, sets the client's price, issues the bill, collects it, and absorbs the gap when a client pays late or not at all while the platform's charge continues. Pricing authority is the reward and the trap: the spread is the operator's to widen with service value or destroy with discounting, and because the client sees one line item, every platform price increase becomes the operator's price increase to defend. Owning the invoice also creates a service expectation the contract may not mention - the client who pays the operator calls the operator when a deposit is wrong - so first-line support capacity has to exist before the first client is billed, not after. The obligations to verify before choosing this rung are program-specific and change: whether the arrangement permits the operator to bill for the platform's service at all, what the operator may call itself in the client's eyes, who is named in the client-facing terms, what happens to clients if the partner agreement terminates, and what the operator's own tax treatment of the resold service is in their jurisdiction. Each of those is verified in the current agreement and with a qualified professional, never inferred from how another program worked.

included: invoice ownership, pricing authority and the spread mechanism
receivable and support obligations created by billing the client
the term classes to verify before adopting the rung, including what happens to clients on termination
excluded: the tax treatment of resold services in a specific jurisdiction, which is a question for the operator's own tax professional
performing the payroll work itself, which is the service-bureau rung
the post-go-live support workflow, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Owning price and invoice converts a program-defined payment into a margin the operator can actually manage with service quality and packaging
pros.example: bundling a monthly review touch into the billed price so the relationship is with the operator rather than with a software vendor

pros.claim: The client relationship is contractually the operator's, which makes the book an asset with defensible continuity rather than a stream of introductions
pros.example: an operator able to move a segment of clients if the platform relationship ends, subject to the agreement's terms

cons.claim: The operator carries collection risk and cash timing risk on a cost that keeps accruing whether or not the client pays
cons.example: a client that stops paying but whose payroll must keep running while the platform charge continues

cons.claim: Every platform price change or outage becomes the operator's to explain, with no ability to point at a third party the client has never met
cons.example: an increase the operator must either absorb or pass on to clients who believe the price is the operator's own

failure_modes: billing clients before first-line support capacity exists
setting a retail price from a competitor's advertised figure rather than from the operator's own cost and service load
assuming the arrangement permits reselling without reading the current agreement's billing and branding terms
ignoring what the agreement says happens to the client book on termination
acceptance_tests: the current partner agreement has been read and the billing permission, branding permission, client-terms naming, and termination-of-book clauses are summarised in the operator's own file

a price build exists that starts from the operator's wholesale cost and service touch-time rather than from a competitor's advertised price, and a collections and dunning process is defined before the first invoice
revisit_triggers: the platform changes wholesale rates, billing permissions or branding rules
receivable ageing deteriorates or a client default occurs
the operator's support load per client exceeds what the spread was built to fund

base.update_signal: the partner agreement's wholesale rate, billing permission, or termination terms are revised, or observed collection performance departs from what the spread assumed

nodes.definition: Run the service-bureau rung as a production operation with dated obligations, because here the operator's hands are on the client's payroll and the client's calendar becomes the operator's calendar. The work is done inside the platform's partner or accountant console: collecting or validating hours and changes, running the pay cycle, reviewing what the platform produced before it is committed, and watching the filing calendar that the platform mostly automates but never owns on the client's behalf. Revenue is the operator's own service fee, which may sit alongside a partner revenue share, and it is earned per client per period rather than per introduction, so the practice compounds and so does the exposure. The capability tests that gate this rung are unglamorous and absolute: coverage when the person who runs payroll is sick during a pay week, a documented review step so a single mistyped rate is caught before it is committed, a defined cut-off discipline with clients so late inputs do not become emergency corrections, and clarity that the operator's role is execution and review rather than professional determination of tax positions. This rung is also the one where the acquisition conversation changes shape: the operator is selling their own reliability rather than software, so proof of process matters more than platform feature lists.

included: what the operator executes and reviews inside the partner console
the coverage, review-step and cut-off capability gates that qualify an operator for this rung
how the sales conversation shifts from software features to the operator's own process
excluded: the detailed per-run and period-end operating rhythm, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base
the initial data migration and parallel run, which belong to the onboarding knowledge base
making tax determinations or representing the client before an agency

pros.claim: Charging for labour rather than for an introduction produces the highest and most durable revenue per client on the ladder, because the client is buying reliability they cannot easily re-source
pros.example: a client who stays through a platform price increase because the person who has run their payroll cleanly for years is the actual product

pros.claim: Being inside the console gives the operator direct visibility of problems early, which converts into both service quality and expansion signal
pros.example: noticing a new hire in an unfamiliar jurisdiction during a run and raising the registration question before it becomes a filing problem

cons.claim: The operator inherits a hard recurring calendar in which lateness is not a service inconvenience but a compliance and payday event
cons.example: an operator taking a holiday during a pay week with no trained backup and a payroll that must still be committed on time

cons.claim: Errors made by the operator's hands land on the client as real money, and the reputational and financial recovery is expensive even when the platform mechanically produced the output
cons.example: a mistyped pay rate committed without review producing an overpayment that must be recovered from an employee

failure_modes: taking on service clients without a second trained person or an agreed contingency
committing a run without an independent review step against the prior period
accepting late client inputs habitually until every period is an emergency
drifting from execution into giving the client tax determinations because the operator is the one who sees the numbers
acceptance_tests: a documented pre-commit review step exists and is evidenced for every serviced client's first periods, including a comparison against the prior period
a written coverage plan names who runs payroll when the primary operator is unavailable, and a cut-off schedule is agreed in writing with each serviced client
revisit_triggers: the serviced client count grows past what the current coverage plan supports
a run error reaches a client, whatever its cause
the platform changes partner console capability or permissions

base.update_signal: an error reaches a client, the serviced book outgrows the coverage plan, or the platform changes what partners may do inside the console

nodes.definition: Understand partner compensation as a mechanism rather than a number, because the figure any given operator earns is produced by a formula in a current agreement that the platform can revise and that differs by program, tier and client. Four payment forms recur and often combine: a one-time introduction payment triggered when a referred client starts and survives a qualifying period; an ongoing share of what the client pays the platform, which continues while stated conditions hold; a wholesale spread between the partner rate and the operator's retail price; and the operator's own service fee, which is not partner compensation at all and is the only component the operator fully controls. The drivers that move the size of the platform-side components are equally mechanical: how many employees the client runs, which add-on modules the client subscribes to, which tier the partner has reached by client count or volume, whether the client came through an attributed path, and how long the client stays. Because all of these are program terms, the discipline is a per-deal verification habit: read the current agreement or partner portal terms at the time of the deal, record what was in force on that date, and never quote a prospect or a referral source a compensation figure from memory or from a public article. Modelling the practice therefore means modelling the mechanism with bands and sensitivities rather than asserting a rate, and stress-testing what happens to the practice if any one component is restructured.

included: the four recurring payment forms and how each is triggered
the drivers that move platform-side compensation
the per-deal verification habit and the dated record of terms in force
excluded: asserting any specific rate, percentage, bounty, tier threshold or platform price as fact
the operator's own tax treatment of partner income, which is a question for their tax professional
the attribution mechanics that decide whether the operator is credited at all, which are handled separately

pros.claim: Modelling the mechanism rather than a number keeps the practice honest and keeps it solvent, because the operator can see immediately which component a program change would remove
pros.example: an operator who knows that most of their income is an ongoing share can test what happens to the practice if the program becomes one-time only

pros.claim: Knowing the drivers reveals where the practice actually grows, which is often client complexity and add-on adoption rather than client count
pros.example: recognising that clients with more employees and more modules move partner-side compensation more than adding another very small client does

cons.claim: Mechanism knowledge does not produce a forecast the operator can bank, so planning stays uncomfortable and lumpy
cons.example: an operator unable to commit to a hire because the compensation form could be restructured at renewal

cons.claim: Per-deal verification is slow and unglamorous, and the temptation to reuse last quarter's understanding is constant
cons.example: quoting a referral source a share arrangement that changed at the program's last revision

failure_modes: stating a compensation figure to a prospect or referral partner from memory
building the entire practice on a single compensation component with no alternative
ignoring qualifying-period conditions so income is recognised before it is actually earned
confusing the operator's own service fee with platform compensation in the practice's numbers
acceptance_tests: a dated extract of the current program's compensation terms exists in the operator's file for the period in which each deal was written
the practice model expresses income as component bands with the drivers named, and contains no figure that cannot be traced to a dated program document or the operator's own price sheet
revisit_triggers: the platform announces or quietly revises program compensation terms
the operator crosses a tier threshold or adds a second platform relationship
actual received compensation diverges from what the mechanism predicted

base.update_signal: the platform publishes revised partner compensation terms, or reconciliation shows received amounts departing from the modelled mechanism

nodes.definition: Treat attribution as the operational heart of partner income, because compensation that is never credited is indistinguishable from work done for free, and credit fails quietly. Programs attribute through a small set of mechanisms - a tracked link, a partner code entered during signup, a lead submitted through a partner portal before the prospect contacts the platform, or an introduction logged by a platform representative - and each fails in a characteristic way: the prospect signs up on a different device or after a tracking window elapses, an office manager completes signup without the code, the prospect had already started a self-serve trial months earlier, or the assigned representative changes and the informal record disappears. The countermeasure is an operator-side ledger recording, per prospect, the date of first introduction, the attribution mechanism used, the evidence that it was used, the platform-side contact, and the date compensation was expected against the date it arrived. Reversal exposure is the ledger's second job: programs commonly attach conditions under which credit can be withheld or reclaimed - early cancellation, non-payment, a qualifying period not met, or an attribution correction - so the operator verifies the current conditions, treats income inside the exposure window as provisional in their own planning, and keeps the evidence that makes a dispute winnable rather than a matter of competing memories.

included: the attribution mechanisms and their characteristic failure paths
the per-prospect ledger fields that make a dispute winnable
reversal and qualifying-period exposure as a planning discipline
excluded: asserting the length or terms of any specific clawback window
the platform's internal crediting systems and their correctness
legal advice on enforcing a partner agreement

pros.claim: A contemporaneous ledger converts an attribution dispute from an argument into a document review, which is the only version the operator can win
pros.example: producing the dated lead submission and the code the prospect confirmed using, when the platform's record shows a self-serve signup

pros.claim: Tracking expected against received compensation reveals systematic leakage that no single missing payment would surface
pros.example: noticing that introductions handed to one representative are credited less often than those submitted through the portal

cons.claim: The ledger is administrative work with no client-visible value, so it is the first discipline abandoned during a busy stretch
cons.example: a quarter of introductions logged only in memory because the operator was in back-to-back meetings

cons.claim: Even perfect evidence does not guarantee credit when the program's own rules put the decision with the platform
cons.example: an introduction that provably preceded a signup but falls outside the program's stated attribution window

failure_modes: sending prospects to the platform before the attribution mechanism is set up and tested
letting a prospect complete signup unattended without confirming the code or link was used
recognising provisional income as certain during the reversal exposure window
keeping no record of which representative or portal an introduction went through
acceptance_tests: the attribution mechanism has been tested end to end with a controlled signup or with the platform's confirmation before any real prospect is sent
every introduction has a ledger entry with date, mechanism, evidence and expected-versus-received compensation, and a periodic reconciliation of the two is performed
revisit_triggers: an expected credit does not arrive or is reversed
the program changes its attribution mechanism, window, or portal
the platform-side representative or partner manager changes

base.update_signal: a credit is missed or reversed, or the program alters its attribution mechanism, window or qualifying conditions

nodes.definition: Evaluate the platform as an operational dependency rather than as a marketing proposition, because the operator is about to lend it their reputation with clients and with referral sources who cannot be re-earned. The evidence classes that matter are behavioural: how the platform handles employment tax filings and deposits and what it states about its role in them; what its published posture is when it makes an error that causes a penalty, and whether that posture is a contractual commitment or a goodwill gesture; how support is actually reached during a pay week and by whom, tested rather than read; what the partner console really allows a partner to see and do; how the platform behaves at period-end when load peaks; which client profiles it genuinely serves and which it declines; and its history of changing partner program terms. Structural questions sit alongside these: whether the operator's whole practice would rest on one platform, what the agreement says happens to the client book on termination, and whether a second platform relationship is permitted for the profiles the first cannot serve. Diligence is time-boxed and evidenced - test the support path, read the current agreement, talk to existing partners about a bad period rather than a good one - and it produces a written disqualifier list so the operator knows in advance which finding stops the partnership rather than discovering it after twenty clients are placed.

included: the behavioural evidence classes to gather about filings, errors, support, console and period-end load
concentration and termination questions about the partner relationship
the written disqualifier list and the time-boxed diligence method
excluded: auditing the platform's internal controls or security architecture
assessing whether the platform's filings are correct for a specific client, which is a professional determination
the operator's own service processes, which the service-bureau rung defines

pros.claim: Testing support and error posture before the first placement prevents the operator's referral sources from being the ones who discover the weakness
pros.example: calling support during a peak period as a partner and timing the response, before promising a CPA that their clients will be looked after

pros.claim: A written disqualifier list makes the decision resistant to a persuasive partner manager, because the standard was set before the relationship existed
pros.example: walking away when the error-and-penalty posture turns out to be discretionary, despite an attractive tier offer

cons.claim: Real evidence about behaviour under stress is hard to obtain before there is a relationship, so early diligence is partly inference
cons.example: having to judge period-end behaviour from other partners' accounts rather than from experience

cons.claim: Thorough diligence delays revenue while competitors are already placing clients
cons.example: spending a season testing and reading while a rival introduces clients and books compensation

failure_modes: reading marketing material and partner-program collateral instead of the current agreement
judging the platform on feature breadth rather than on how it behaves when something goes wrong
ignoring the termination-of-book clause because the relationship is new and friendly
committing the whole practice to one platform without checking whether a second relationship is permitted
acceptance_tests: a diligence file exists containing the dated current agreement extract, a tested support-response record, notes from at least one existing partner about a bad period, and the console capability check
a written disqualifier list was recorded before the diligence began and each item is marked as met, not met, or unresolved
revisit_triggers: the platform changes partner terms, support model, or console permissions
clients or referral sources report a pattern of service failures
the practice's dependence on one platform crosses the operator's stated concentration comfort

base.update_signal: the platform revises partner terms or support structure, or accumulated client and referral-source experience contradicts a diligence finding

nodes.definition: Build a short, repeatable profile of the prospect's payroll before any recommendation, because payroll complexity is not proportional to headcount and the dimensions that decide fit are invisible unless asked for. The dimensions that repeatedly change the answer are: employee count against contractor count and how the prospect distinguishes them; the jurisdictions where people actually work rather than where the business is registered; pay frequency and whether different groups are paid differently; pay composition, including hourly with overtime, salary, tips, commissions, piece rates, bonuses and reimbursements; deduction and contribution classes present, such as retirement plans, health premiums, garnishments and union dues; special regimes the prospect operates under, such as certified or prevailing wage work, agricultural or household employment, or multi-entity and common-paymaster arrangements; time-tracking and accounting systems that must connect; and the growth trajectory that will change all of the above within a year. The profile is collected in aggregate form, scored coarsely as simple, moderate or complex against the platform's demonstrated capability, and kept as the artifact that later justifies the fit decision, the price, and the timeline. The discipline it enforces is refusal to quote before the profile exists, because in this business the expensive surprises are structural rather than numerical.

included: the intake dimensions that drive fit, effort and timeline
coarse complexity scoring against demonstrated platform capability
the rule that no quote or timeline precedes the profile
excluded: collecting employee-level records, which is post-signature onboarding work
determining whether a worker is correctly classified, which is a professional determination handled by triage and referral
the migration and setup plan itself, which belongs to the onboarding knowledge base

pros.claim: A structured profile turns a fit decision into a comparison against known platform capability rather than an optimistic guess
pros.example: surfacing prevailing-wage work in a construction prospect before promising anything, rather than during implementation

pros.claim: The same profile is the honest basis for price and timeline, so the commercial conversation stops depending on the prospect's own estimate of their simplicity
pros.example: a prospect who described themselves as simple turning out to run three pay groups across two jurisdictions with garnishments

cons.claim: A structured intake feels like an interrogation to a small owner who expected a quick answer, and some will disengage
cons.example: an owner with four employees who wanted a price in one message and instead received a dozen questions

cons.claim: Self-reported answers are often wrong in predictable directions, especially about worker classification and where people actually work
cons.example: an owner reporting one jurisdiction while two staff have quietly relocated and work remotely from another

failure_modes: quoting a price or a go-live date before the profile exists
accepting the prospect's self-description of simplicity without probing pay composition
asking for the profile in employee-level detail instead of aggregates
profiling the business as it is today and ignoring a known hiring plan
acceptance_tests: every quoted prospect has a completed profile covering worker counts, work jurisdictions, pay frequency and composition, deduction classes, special regimes, connected systems and growth plan
the profile carries a coarse complexity score with the specific dimension that drove the score named
revisit_triggers: the prospect reports a hire in a new jurisdiction or a new pay type before signature
discovery surfaces a special regime not covered by the current intake form
the platform's demonstrated capability changes, altering what counts as complex

base.update_signal: repeated post-signature surprises reveal a dimension the intake form does not ask about, or the platform's capability set changes what the score means

nodes.definition: Know the classes of employer registration and tax-account obligation that sit underneath any payroll deal, so their presence can be surfaced during acquisition without ever asserting a jurisdiction's specifics. The recurring classes are a national or federal employer identifier; a jurisdiction-level wage withholding account for each place where employees actually work; an unemployment or social insurance employer account, typically with an experience-based contribution rate assigned to the employer; local or municipal taxes that exist in some places and not others; industry or programme-specific registrations such as those attaching to certified or prevailing wage work; and the third-party authorisation class that governs whether a platform or agent may file, deposit or access an account on the employer's behalf. What the operator needs during acquisition is not the content of these rules but their shape: which classes are implicated by the prospect's actual work locations, whether the prospect already holds each account or must obtain it, roughly how long obtaining one tends to take relative to the prospect's desired start date, and who will do that work. Every specific - name, threshold, rate, deadline, procedure, and whether an obligation exists at all - is flagged with an explicit instruction to verify current rules in that jurisdiction with a qualified professional, because these differ by place and change, and because a confident wrong answer here is the kind that produces assessed penalties.

included: the recurring classes of employer registration and account obligation
identifying which classes a prospect's work locations implicate and whether accounts already exist
the verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction instruction attached to every specific
excluded: stating any jurisdiction's thresholds, rates, deadlines, form identifiers or procedures as fact
actually performing registrations or executing third-party authorisations, which belongs to the onboarding knowledge base
advising whether a particular registration is required for a particular employer

pros.claim: Naming the classes lets the operator predict which deals are slow before promising a start date, since missing accounts govern the critical path
pros.example: discovering during discovery that a prospect with remote staff in a second jurisdiction holds no withholding account there, and adjusting the timeline instead of the promise

pros.claim: Class-level fluency signals competence to accountants and bookkeepers, who evaluate a payroll partner mostly on whether they know what they do not know
pros.example: a bookkeeper deciding to refer after hearing the operator route a specific rate question to the client's own professional while explaining the account class clearly

cons.claim: Class-level knowledge is easy to over-extend into specifics under a prospect's pressure for a definite answer
cons.example: an operator who has seen one jurisdiction's registration flow assuming the neighbouring one works the same way

cons.claim: Surfacing registration obligations can stall a deal by revealing work the prospect did not know they owed
cons.example: a prospect pausing to consult their accountant after learning that a remote hire may implicate another jurisdiction's accounts

failure_modes: stating a deadline, rate or threshold from memory or from another jurisdiction
assuming the platform handles a registration that the employer must obtain itself
missing the third-party authorisation class and discovering at cutover that filings cannot be made
profiling registrations from the business address rather than from where employees actually work
acceptance_tests: for each prospect, the implicated obligation classes are listed against actual work locations with a held-or-needed marker per class
no client-facing statement asserts a jurisdiction-specific rule without an accompanying instruction to verify current rules with a qualified professional in that jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: the prospect adds a work location or a remote employee in a new jurisdiction
a registration takes materially longer than the timeline assumed
the platform changes which registrations or authorisations it supports

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction changes its registration or third-party authorisation regime, or a deal reveals an obligation class the current list does not name

nodes.definition: Recognise worker classification exposure as a signal during acquisition and route it rather than resolve it, because whether a given worker is an employee or a contractor is a legal determination with tests that vary by jurisdiction and by programme, and it is the single most consequential question an unqualified party can answer wrongly. The signals are easy to spot in discovery: a prospect who says everyone is on contractor paperwork, who describes people working fixed hours under direction with tools the business supplies, who converted staff to contractors to reduce cost, who mixes the same role across both categories, or who asks the operator to help keep people off payroll. The correct handling has three parts. First, do not rule: the operator names the class of question and the fact that determinations depend on jurisdiction-specific tests, and refers the prospect to a qualified professional in writing. Second, do not build a proposal that depends on a classification the operator has been told is under question, because a later correction reprices and re-times the whole engagement. Third, treat the prospect's response as qualification data: an owner who wants a professional opinion is a good client, and an owner who wants a vendor to help them avoid one is a liability the practice should decline, politely and without lecturing.

included: the discovery signals that indicate classification exposure
the name-and-refer response and its written form
using the prospect's reaction as a qualification and decline signal
excluded: making or endorsing any classification determination
explaining a jurisdiction's classification tests as if they were general rules
remediation of past classification decisions, which is professional work for the client's own advisers

pros.claim: Routing rather than ruling protects the operator from the largest liability available in this business while still adding value the prospect can feel
pros.example: handing a prospect a written note that the question needs their own professional, which the prospect later describes as the moment they trusted the operator

pros.claim: The reaction is a fast, reliable filter for client quality, which saves the practice from its worst accounts before any work is done
pros.example: a prospect who responds to the referral suggestion by asking whether the operator can just run everyone as contractors, revealing a client to decline

cons.claim: Declining on classification grounds forfeits revenue that a less careful competitor will collect
cons.example: watching a prospect sign elsewhere after being told their arrangement needs a professional opinion first

cons.claim: Raising the topic can offend an owner who believes their arrangement is settled and reads the question as an accusation
cons.example: a long-established business hearing the question as a suggestion that they have been doing it wrong for years

failure_modes: offering an opinion on a specific worker because the answer felt obvious
designing the proposal and pricing around a classification that is under question
ignoring the signal to keep the deal alive
lecturing the prospect instead of naming the class and referring out
acceptance_tests: every prospect showing a classification signal has a written referral note on file, with no operator opinion on the determination recorded anywhere
no proposal or price in the pipeline depends on a worker categorisation the operator was told is under review
revisit_triggers: a prospect or client reports an agency inquiry or audit touching classification
a jurisdiction's classification framework is publicly revised
a proposal is found built on an unresolved classification assumption

base.update_signal: a jurisdiction revises its classification tests or enforcement posture, or a client experiences an inquiry that shows the triage signals were incomplete

nodes.definition: Decide fit by comparing the complexity profile against what the platform has demonstrably done, and be willing to say no, because a payroll misfit is not a disappointing purchase but a recurring operational failure that surfaces every pay period and lands on the client's employees. The match is made dimension by dimension: does the platform handle these pay compositions, these deduction classes, these work jurisdictions, this special regime, this accounting or time-tracking connection, and this scale trajectory - and is the evidence a demonstration or a salesperson's assurance. Three outcomes are legitimate. A clear fit proceeds. A conditional fit proceeds with the limitation stated in writing to the prospect before signature, so the constraint is a known trade rather than a later discovery. A misfit is declined, with a specific reason and, where the operator can honestly give one, a direction toward a product class that does serve the profile - even when that means no compensation for the operator on this deal. The rule that makes the whole node work is that a compensation difference between options may never decide a fit question; where two platforms both genuinely fit, the operator may choose the one they support best and must disclose the relationship, and where only one fits, fit wins regardless of what it pays.

included: the dimension-by-dimension capability comparison and evidence standard
the fit, conditional-fit and decline outcomes and how each is communicated
the rule that compensation never decides a fit question
excluded: ranking named commercial platforms or making product recommendations outside a specific client's profile
the implementation of the chosen platform, which belongs to the onboarding knowledge base
advising the client on the tax consequences of any platform's handling

pros.claim: Declining a misfit protects the referral channel, which is worth far more than the forfeited deal because a bad placement is discussed by the referring professional with everyone they know
pros.example: declining a construction prospect needing certified payroll and keeping the referring bookkeeper's confidence for the next five ordinary clients

pros.claim: Writing conditional-fit limitations down converts a future complaint into a documented trade the client accepted
pros.example: stating before signature that a particular report the client uses will have to be produced manually each period

cons.claim: Honest declines cost immediate revenue and are hardest to make in exactly the months when the pipeline is thin
cons.example: turning away the only live deal in a quiet stretch because the platform cannot serve the client's special regime

cons.claim: Capability evidence is often incomplete, so a conditional fit can be judged on a demonstration that does not survive real production volume
cons.example: a connection that works in a demonstration but proves fragile at period-end

failure_modes: accepting a salesperson's assurance as capability evidence
letting the compensation difference between two options decide the recommendation
communicating a conditional fit verbally so it is remembered as a promise of full capability
declining without giving the prospect any honest direction, which wastes the goodwill the decline earned
acceptance_tests: each deal file records the capability comparison per profile dimension with the evidence type used, and the resulting fit, conditional-fit or decline outcome
every conditional fit has a written limitation statement acknowledged by the prospect before signature
revisit_triggers: the platform adds or removes a capability that changes a previously recorded outcome
a placed client hits a limitation that the match did not predict
a decline pattern concentrates in one profile type, indicating a second platform relationship may be needed

base.update_signal: the platform's demonstrated capability set changes, or placed clients reveal capability gaps the comparison did not capture

nodes.definition: Map who is standing next to a small employer at the moment payroll becomes a problem, because payroll is rarely bought from an advertisement and is almost always changed on somebody's recommendation. The productive source classes are distinguishable by motive rather than by title: bookkeepers and accounting professionals, who feel payroll risk directly and often want it out of their own hands; tax practitioners, who meet the consequences of bad payroll at filing time; insurance producers, especially those writing workers compensation where premium is calculated from actual payroll and a platform connection creates a direct interest; benefits brokers, whose deduction setups depend on payroll behaving; business bankers and lenders, who see new entities forming and first hires happening; human-resources consultants and fractional operators, who arrive exactly when a business starts formalising; industry associations, franchise networks and chambers, which offer reach at the cost of a slower and more institutional sale; and existing clients, whose peer introductions convert best of all. Each class is worked differently and pays back on a different clock, so the portfolio is managed like an allocation: a small number of deep relationships that produce steady flow, a wider set of low-maintenance contacts, and a stated rule against depending on a single source whose retirement or change of firm would end the pipeline. What every class wants in return is the same thing and it is not money first: certainty that their client will be looked after and that their own relationship will not be taken.

included: the source classes and the motive that makes each one refer
portfolio management across deep and wide relationships and single-source dependence limits
what referral sources want in return beyond compensation
excluded: the written terms and fee-sharing restrictions of a partner arrangement, which are handled separately
buying lead lists or contact data in place of relationships
post-sale client communication, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Referred payroll prospects arrive pre-qualified and pre-trusted, which shortens a sale that otherwise fights heavy incumbent inertia
pros.example: a bookkeeper's introduction that skips the entire credibility phase because the owner already trusts the person making it

pros.claim: A portfolio of source classes smooths the seasonality of a business whose closes cluster around calendar boundaries
pros.example: banker introductions of newly formed businesses arriving through the year while established-business switches cluster at year-end

cons.claim: Channel building pays back slowly and unevenly, so it competes badly with direct outreach for an operator who needs revenue soon
cons.example: months of relationship work with an accounting firm before the first client is handed over

cons.claim: A source's own reputation is at stake in every introduction, so a single bad outcome can close a channel permanently
cons.example: one poorly handled implementation ending a relationship that had been producing steady introductions

failure_modes: treating every source class the same way with one generic approach
depending on one prolific source for most of the pipeline
asking for referrals before demonstrating anything the source can vouch for
going silent about a referred client so the source learns the outcome from their own client
acceptance_tests: a written channel map lists the source classes being worked, the named relationships in each, the motive assumed for each class, and the current contribution of each to closed clients
no single source accounts for more of the pipeline than the operator's stated concentration limit, or the breach is recorded with a remediation plan
revisit_triggers: a major source retires, changes firm, or stops referring
one class stops producing or produces consistently poor-fit prospects
the operator's niche or engagement rung changes, altering which classes are relevant

base.update_signal: observed closed-client attribution by source class diverges from the assumed motive map, or a channel stops producing

nodes.definition: Work the bookkeeping and accounting relationship as the deepest vein in payroll referral, because these professionals hold the exact combination that produces referrals: they touch payroll data monthly, they carry the risk of getting it wrong, they usually dislike the work, and their clients ask them who to use. The economics from their side are the argument to make: payroll is a high-frequency, deadline-bound, penalty-adjacent task that often prices poorly relative to the anxiety it causes, and handing it to a specialist converts it from exposure into either a clean referral or a service they can stop performing. The alliance is built on demonstration rather than persuasion - one client handled visibly well is worth more than any presentation - and it is kept open by a covenant that must be explicit: the operator will not solicit the bookkeeping, tax or advisory work that belongs to the referring professional, will report back on referred clients at agreed points, will flag anything found that belongs to the professional's domain rather than acting on it, and will never put the professional in a position of having recommended a failure. The single most common way this vein is closed is a payroll partner quietly expanding into the referrer's own service line, which ends not just that relationship but its word-of-mouth radius among a professional community that talks to itself constantly.

included: why accounting professionals refer payroll and how the case is made from their economics
the do-not-poach covenant and the reporting-back rhythm
demonstration-first relationship building
excluded: fee-sharing terms and the restrictions that may prevent a licensed professional from accepting compensation, which are handled separately
expansion into adjacent recurring services, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base
advising the professional on their own practice, pricing or obligations

pros.claim: One productive accounting relationship can supply a steady stream of pre-qualified prospects with the trust already transferred
pros.example: a bookkeeping firm handing over its payroll clients in a sequence as each one reaches a natural switching moment

pros.claim: These professionals pre-filter complexity better than any other channel because they have already seen the client's actual numbers
pros.example: a referrer warning in advance about a client's garnishment and multi-jurisdiction situation, so the fit judgement starts from reality

cons.claim: The covenant permanently forecloses the most natural expansion path, since the adjacent bookkeeping work is exactly what the referrer does
cons.example: declining a serviced client's request to take over their bookkeeping because the referring firm sent them

cons.claim: These relationships are slow to build and are protected carefully, so an operator without a demonstrable track record has little to trade
cons.example: a new operator unable to name a single client the firm can call for a reference

failure_modes: pitching the alliance on the operator's compensation rather than on the referrer's risk relief
accepting the referred client's invitation to expand into the referrer's service line
