failing to report back, so the referrer learns about problems from their own client
treating the referrer as a lead source rather than as an ongoing professional relationship
acceptance_tests: a written referral understanding with each accounting relationship states the do-not-solicit scope, the reporting-back points, and how findings in the referrer's domain are handed back
referred clients have a report-back record at the agreed points, and any request to expand into the referrer's scope is documented as declined or explicitly released by the referrer
revisit_triggers: a referred client asks the operator to take over work belonging to the referrer
the referring firm changes ownership, staffing or service scope
a referred client has a poor experience the referrer has not yet been told about

base.update_signal: a referring firm changes its own service scope or ownership, or referral flow from accounting relationships changes materially in either direction

nodes.definition: Choose a small number of industries to concentrate in, because payroll expertise does not generalise cheaply but compounds ferociously within a vertical. Each industry carries a characteristic quirk set - tipped wages and tip pooling in food service, crew scheduling and overtime patterns in home services and trades, prevailing or certified wage regimes in public-works construction, clinician mixes and per-diem arrangements in healthcare practices, seasonal and variable-hours workforces in retail and hospitality, grant-restricted funding and allocation in nonprofits - and learning one set well converts every later prospect in that vertical from a research project into a recognition. Concentration pays three ways: the discovery conversation gets sharper because the operator asks about the quirk before the prospect mentions it, the fit judgement gets faster because the platform's capability against that quirk set has already been tested, and referral flow accelerates because a vertical is a community whose members talk to each other and to a shared set of advisers. The costs are real: concentration means correlated exposure to one industry's downturn, a narrower total market, and the risk of committing to a vertical whose quirks the operator's platform serves badly, which is why niche selection is validated against platform capability before collateral is built rather than after.

included: how vertical quirk sets compound into acquisition speed
validating a candidate niche against demonstrated platform capability before committing
the concentration costs and how many verticals to run
excluded: stating market sizes, industry counts or growth rates for any vertical
the operational handling of a vertical's quirks after go-live, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base
giving industry-specific wage-and-hour or tax guidance, which is professional advice

pros.claim: Vertical fluency shortens discovery dramatically because the operator names the prospect's own complications before being told about them
pros.example: asking a restaurant owner how tip pooling is currently allocated, which immediately separates the operator from a generalist

pros.claim: A vertical is a referral network in itself, so satisfied clients and shared advisers compound introductions inside it
pros.example: one dental practice introduction leading to others through a shared practice-management adviser

cons.claim: Concentration correlates the whole book's risk to one industry's conditions and to one regime's rule changes
cons.example: a practice built on hospitality clients facing simultaneous pressure across the book during an industry downturn

cons.claim: Committing to a vertical whose quirks the platform serves poorly builds an acquisition engine that feeds deals the operator must decline
cons.example: specialising in public-works construction and then finding the certified-wage requirement unsupported

failure_modes: choosing a niche from personal interest without testing platform capability against its quirk set
spreading across too many verticals so no quirk set is ever learned deeply
building collateral and positioning before the niche is validated
ignoring how correlated the niche makes the book's risk
acceptance_tests: each chosen vertical has a written quirk list and a recorded capability test of the platform against each quirk, dated and with the evidence type noted
the number of concurrent verticals is stated and justified against the operator's capacity to keep each quirk list current
revisit_triggers: a rule change or industry shift alters a vertical's quirk set
the platform gains or loses capability relevant to a chosen vertical
decline rates rise inside a chosen vertical, indicating a capability mismatch

base.update_signal: a vertical's regulatory or operating conditions change, or observed decline rates inside a niche reveal a platform capability mismatch

nodes.definition: Put referral arrangements in writing and verify, before promising anything, whether the person on the other side may lawfully or professionally accept what is being offered, because compensation arrangements with regulated professionals are governed by rules the operator does not control and may not even be subject to themselves. The restriction classes that recur are: professional-body rules on accepting commissions or contingent fees, which in some bodies require disclosure to the client, restrict acceptance where an independence or attest relationship exists, or prohibit it outright; insurance regulation on producer compensation and inducements, which constrains what an insurance producer may accept or pass on; employer and firm policies that forbid staff from accepting outside compensation; and platform program terms that may restrict onward sharing of partner compensation. In every case the discipline is the same: name the class, ask the professional to confirm their own position with their body or compliance function, and record the answer before the first introduction rather than after the first payment. The written arrangement itself then fixes a small number of things that otherwise become disputes: what triggers a share and when it is paid, what happens if credit is reversed, who discloses what to the client, what each party may and may not solicit from the other's clients, how the arrangement ends and what happens to clients already introduced, and how confidential client information is handled between the parties.

included: the restriction classes that may prevent a source from accepting a share
the verify-before-promising sequence and the recorded confirmation
the terms a written referral arrangement must fix, including termination and confidentiality
excluded: determining whether a specific arrangement is permissible for a specific licensee, which is a question for their own body, compliance function or counsel
drafting an enforceable contract, which is legal work
asserting any jurisdiction's or body's specific rule as fact

pros.claim: Verifying first prevents the worst version of this failure, which is a professional accepting compensation they were not permitted to accept on the operator's assurance
pros.example: a referring practitioner checking with their professional body before any arrangement is signed, and the operator restructuring to a non-compensated arrangement when the answer is restrictive

pros.claim: Fixing termination and client-solicitation terms in advance stops the predictable end-of-relationship dispute over introduced clients
pros.example: an arrangement that says clearly what happens to already-introduced clients if the parties stop working together

cons.claim: Requiring written arrangements slows relationship building and can feel like distrust to a professional who wanted an informal understanding
cons.example: a long-standing contact who preferred a handshake and cools when a document appears

cons.claim: Verification often returns an unhelpful answer, leaving the operator to build a non-compensated referral relationship that is harder to sustain
cons.example: a practitioner permitted to refer but not to accept anything, so reciprocity has to be built from non-monetary value

failure_modes: promising a share before the source has confirmed they may accept it
relying on how another professional in a different body or jurisdiction was permitted to be paid
leaving termination and client-solicitation terms unwritten
sharing client information between parties without an agreed confidentiality basis
acceptance_tests: each compensated referral relationship has a written arrangement covering trigger, payment timing, reversal handling, disclosure duties, solicitation limits, termination and confidentiality
a recorded confirmation exists from each regulated source that they have checked their own position, dated before the first introduction
revisit_triggers: a professional body, regulator, or the platform program changes rules on compensation sharing
a source changes firm, role, or licensure status
a compensation reversal occurs that the arrangement does not address

base.update_signal: a professional body, insurance regulator, or partner program revises compensation-sharing rules, or a source's licensure or employment status changes

nodes.definition: Learn the events that actually move a small employer off an incumbent payroll arrangement, because dissatisfaction alone almost never does it. Payroll is high-switching-cost infrastructure: it works most weeks, the data is embedded, the owner does not understand it well enough to feel safe changing it, and the person who would run the change is the busiest person in the business. The trigger classes that break that inertia are observable: an agency notice, penalty or interest assessment; a visible failure such as a late or wrong pay run or a missed filing; a price increase that arrives without a matching service change; the loss of the person who was doing it, whether an internal bookkeeper leaving or an external provider retiring; growth past the current arrangement, especially a first employee, a first hire in a new jurisdiction, or a first benefits or retirement plan; a change of ownership, entity restructure or acquisition; an audit or funding event that forces the records to be defensible; a systems change elsewhere, such as new accounting or time-tracking software that must connect; and the calendar itself, which forces a decision at year-end whether or not anything is broken. The operating implication is a prospecting posture rather than a persuasion posture: find businesses standing in a trigger, ask questions that would surface one if it exists, and stay in patient contact with those that have none, because manufacturing urgency in a compliance-adjacent purchase is both ineffective and unethical.

included: the trigger classes and their observable signals
the find-do-not-manufacture prospecting posture
patient nurture of trigger-free prospects
excluded: fear-based framing of compliance risk, which is explicitly prohibited
the timing decision about when a triggered prospect should actually cut over
post-sale retention dynamics, which belong to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Trigger-led prospecting concentrates effort on the small share of businesses that can actually move now, which is the difference between a working pipeline and a grind
pros.example: a bookkeeper mentioning that a client just received an agency notice, which is a live conversation rather than a cold one

pros.claim: The trigger map doubles as a referral-source briefing, because sources cannot spot opportunities they have not been told to look for
pros.example: asking an insurance producer to mention any client who just hired in a second jurisdiction

cons.claim: Waiting for triggers makes the pipeline lumpy and largely outside the operator's control, which is uncomfortable to plan around
cons.example: a quiet stretch where nothing in the territory is breaking and no one is hiring

cons.claim: Some triggers arrive as distress, and working them requires restraint precisely when the prospect is most persuadable
cons.example: an owner frightened by a penalty notice who would agree to anything put in front of them

failure_modes: pitching businesses that have no trigger and calling the resulting silence a market problem
inventing urgency where no trigger exists
failing to brief referral sources on which signals to watch for
abandoning trigger-free prospects entirely instead of nurturing them toward the next boundary
acceptance_tests: every active pipeline opportunity records the observed trigger and the evidence for it, and opportunities with no trigger are held in a nurture track rather than pushed
referral sources have received a short written list of the signals to watch for in their own client base
revisit_triggers: close rates fall despite triggers being recorded, suggesting the map is mis-specified
a new trigger class appears repeatedly in won deals
a platform or market change alters which triggers matter

base.update_signal: won-deal analysis shows trigger classes absent from the map or shows recorded triggers failing to predict closes

nodes.definition: Run the pipeline against the calendar that actually governs payroll changes, because when a client can switch is a harder constraint than whether they want to. A change effective at the start of a new tax year is the cheapest, since the new provider starts from zero accumulated balances and the outgoing provider completes the year's reporting obligations for the wages it processed. A change at a quarter boundary is the usual second-best, because period-level reporting closes cleanly even though year-to-date figures still have to be carried across. A mid-period change is the most expensive: balances must be migrated and reconciled mid-stream, two providers each hold part of the year, reporting reconciliation becomes an explicit project, and the risk of a duplicated or missed obligation rises. Three operating consequences follow. First, lead time: because the boundary is fixed and setup and registration work is not instant, the conversation that produces a start-of-year cutover has to begin well before the boundary, which makes the busiest selling period sit uncomfortably ahead of the busiest delivery period. Second, parking discipline: a good-fit prospect discovered too close to a boundary is better parked with a scheduled return than pushed into a rushed cutover the operator will regret. Third, honest counsel: telling a prospect to stay where they are until the boundary is frequently the correct advice and is remembered as such. The exception is a live failure - accruing exposure, missed filings, or a provider that has stopped functioning - where waiting costs more than moving.

included: why boundary cutovers are cheaper and what a mid-period change adds
the lead-time consequence for pipeline building and the parking discipline
the conditions under which breaking the calendar is the right advice
excluded: executing the cutover, balance migration and parallel run, which belong to the onboarding knowledge base
asserting specific filing deadlines, period definitions or reporting rules for any jurisdiction
the ongoing period-end compliance calendar after go-live, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Timing to a boundary removes an entire class of migration risk from the engagement before it starts, which is the cheapest risk reduction available
pros.example: a start-of-year cutover where no partial-year balances have to be carried across at all

pros.claim: Recommending a wait builds durable credibility and usually converts, because the prospect experiences advice that cost the operator something
pros.example: a prospect who was told to stay until the boundary returning at that boundary without shopping around again

cons.claim: The calendar concentrates both closes and implementations into narrow windows, straining capacity exactly when errors are most expensive
cons.example: several clients all requiring start-of-year cutover in the same short period

cons.claim: Parked deals decay, because a prospect's urgency fades and competitors or the incumbent can act during the wait
cons.example: a spring-parked prospect who has forgotten the conversation by the time the boundary arrives

failure_modes: closing a mid-period switch for revenue timing when nothing was broken
starting boundary conversations too late for the registration work the profile requires
parking a prospect with no scheduled return, which is abandonment with extra steps
treating the boundary rule as absolute when a client is accruing real exposure now
acceptance_tests: every open opportunity carries a target cutover boundary and a backward-planned date for the decision that boundary requires, accounting for registration lead time
each mid-period cutover in the pipeline has a written justification naming the live failure that makes waiting worse than moving
revisit_triggers: a prospect's exposure changes while they are parked
capacity at a boundary is over-committed relative to the parked pipeline
registration or setup lead times prove longer than the backward plan assumed

base.update_signal: observed cutovers show registration or setup lead times different from the backward plan, or boundary-period capacity repeatedly fails

nodes.definition: Run discovery as a structured interview whose purpose is a decision rather than a close, because in payroll the operator's credibility comes from asking better questions than the incumbent ever did. The sequence that works moves from situation to evidence to consequence to timing: who touches payroll today and how long it takes them; what the current arrangement is and what it costs, asked in a way that invites the prospect to look rather than recall; what has actually gone wrong, with the prospect's own artifacts as evidence - a notice they received, a correction they had to make, a report they cannot get; who else is affected, since employees experiencing late or wrong pay is the consequence owners feel most; what would have to be true to change, and when their calendar realistically allows it. Two disciplines run through the whole conversation. The first is evidence over assertion: the operator's claims about the prospect's situation come from documents the prospect volunteered, not from generalisations about their industry. The second is restraint: the operator does not supply consequences the prospect did not experience, does not quantify penalties, and does not press an owner who is visibly overwhelmed - in that case the right move is to slow down, put the summary in writing, and let them consult whoever they trust. Discovery ends with a written summary of what was heard, which is both the qualification artifact and the first demonstration of how the operator works.

included: the situation-evidence-consequence-timing question sequence
the evidence-over-assertion and restraint disciplines
the written discovery summary as the qualification artifact
excluded: collecting employee-level data or credentials during the conversation
quantifying the prospect's penalty exposure or making compliance predictions
the fit and platform recommendation itself, which is a separate decision made from the profile

pros.claim: A structured interview surfaces the operator's actual differentiator, which is understanding the prospect's situation rather than describing software
pros.example: an owner realising during the questions how many hours a month payroll costs their office manager, without being told

pros.claim: The written summary creates a shared factual basis that makes the later proposal short and hard to argue with
pros.example: a proposal that simply responds point by point to the prospect's own stated problems

cons.claim: Discovery is expensive in unpaid time and a share of it lands on prospects who will never buy
cons.example: a full interview with an owner who was gathering comparison material for their incumbent's renewal negotiation

cons.claim: Prospects frequently misreport what they pay and what goes wrong, so evidence has to be requested carefully without implying distrust
cons.example: an owner certain their payroll costs a small fixed amount until they look at the actual invoice

failure_modes: presenting before understanding, so the pitch answers problems the prospect does not have
accepting recalled figures instead of asking the prospect to look at their own documents
pushing through visible overwhelm to reach a commitment in the same conversation
letting the conversation collect sensitive employee detail that the qualification does not need
acceptance_tests: each qualified opportunity has a written discovery summary covering current arrangement, evidenced problems, affected parties, decision maker and timing constraint
no discovery record contains employee-level identifiers, wage detail for named individuals, or credentials
revisit_triggers: won and lost deals show a question that should have been asked and was not
the platform or engagement rung changes what discovery must establish
a prospect discloses distress or pressure that requires the conversation to be slowed

base.update_signal: loss analysis identifies a recurring unasked question, or discovery records are found holding data the qualification did not require

nodes.definition: Discuss compliance risk in a way that informs a decision instead of manufacturing dread, because payroll sits next to penalties and interest and is therefore unusually easy to sell with fear - which produces bad purchases, resentful clients, and a practice that cannot look its referral sources in the eye. The permitted register is specific: describe mechanisms in class terms, such as the fact that late deposits and late filings generally attract penalty and interest regimes whose specifics differ by jurisdiction and must be verified; use the prospect's own documents, such as a notice they actually received, as the only case-specific evidence; and answer questions about exposure by referring the prospect to a qualified professional who can assess their situation. The prohibited register is equally specific: no invented or quoted penalty figures, no implied audit probability, no anecdotes about businesses destroyed by payroll errors, no suggestion that the operator or the platform prevents penalties as such, and no time-limited pressure attached to a compliance claim. A vulnerable-operator rule sits on top: when a prospect is in distress, unwell, grieving, in a business crisis, or plainly out of their depth, the operator slows down, puts things in writing, encourages them to involve someone they trust, and declines to take a same-day commitment. The rule costs deals and it is the reason the practice can hold a referral network for years.

included: the permitted class-level register for discussing compliance risk
the prohibited framings, including invented figures, audit-probability claims and urgency attached to risk
the vulnerable-operator slow-down rule
excluded: assessing a specific prospect's penalty exposure, which is professional work
asserting any jurisdiction's penalty amounts, interest rates or enforcement statistics
post-sale incident communication, which belongs to the recurring-relationship knowledge base

pros.claim: Class-level honesty is more persuasive with the audience that matters, because accountants and bookkeepers immediately recognise and distrust fear-selling
pros.example: a referring professional continuing to send clients precisely because the operator refused to put a number on their client's exposure

pros.claim: The vulnerable-operator rule prevents the worst outcome in this business, which is a distressed owner signing something they did not understand
pros.example: postponing a signature with an owner managing a family emergency and confirming the decision in writing a week later

cons.claim: Restraint loses deals to competitors willing to frighten prospects into signing
cons.example: a prospect signing elsewhere after being shown a dramatic penalty presentation the operator would not make

cons.claim: Under-stating risk can leave a prospect genuinely unaware of a real problem, so the discipline must inform rather than merely avoid
cons.example: an owner who does not act on a notice because the conversation was so careful that nothing registered

failure_modes: quoting a penalty figure or an audit likelihood to make a point
attaching a deadline to a compliance claim to force a decision
using another business's disaster story as a selling device
continuing to press a prospect who is visibly overwhelmed or in distress
acceptance_tests: all client-facing material and call notes are free of specific penalty figures, audit-probability claims, and urgency framings tied to compliance risk
at least one documented instance exists of a decision being deliberately slowed or a commitment declined under the vulnerable-operator rule, showing the rule is real in practice
revisit_triggers: a prospect or referral source describes the conversation as pressuring
new sales collateral or a new person joins the sales conversation
a competitor's framing tempts the operator to match it

base.update_signal: a complaint, referral-source comment, or internal review finds pressure or fear framing in the sales conversation or collateral

nodes.definition: Present the offer as two clearly separated things and build the operator's own number from the operator's own economics, because the most common commercial failure in this business is a blended price that hides which part is software and which part is the operator's labour. The platform subscription is the client's cost for the software and the filing service, set by the platform or by the operator's retail policy on the reseller rung; the service layer is what the operator personally does, and it is the only part whose price the operator can defend from first principles. That price is built mechanically: count the touch points in a period, estimate the realistic time each takes for this complexity profile, add the period-end and year-end touches that arrive on a calendar rather than weekly, add a contingency for the corrections that occur in any real book, apply the operator's own required hourly economics, and only then compare the result with what the market appears to bear as a sanity check rather than as the source. The scope statement that accompanies the price is equally commercial: what is included per period, what is explicitly not included, what happens when the client is late with inputs, what an out-of-scope request costs, and which situations trigger a re-price - a jurisdiction added, headcount crossing a stated band, a new pay type. Detailed operational division of duties after go-live belongs to onboarding; what is fixed here is the commercial promise the client is buying.

included: separation of platform subscription from the operator's service layer in the offer
the touch-time and complexity build that produces the operator's own price
the commercial scope statement, exclusions and re-price triggers
excluded: asserting any price point, rate, or market figure as fact
the operational responsibility matrix between platform, service layer and client after go-live, which belongs to the onboarding knowledge base
the operator's own tax treatment of the fees charged

pros.claim: Separating the two components makes a platform price change survivable, because the client can see which part moved and why
pros.example: a subscription increase that does not become an argument about the operator's own fee

pros.claim: Pricing from touch time makes complex clients profitable instead of quietly subsidised by simple ones
pros.example: a multi-jurisdiction client with several pay types priced from the work it actually generates rather than from a headcount band

cons.claim: A two-part price is harder to compare against an all-in competitor quote and can look more expensive at a glance
cons.example: a prospect comparing the operator's separated figures against a single blended number from a rival

cons.claim: Touch-time estimates are unreliable until the operator has real book data, so early prices are systematically wrong in one direction or the other
cons.example: a first-year practice underestimating the correction load a real client generates

failure_modes: copying a competitor's price and reverse-engineering a scope to fit it
blending platform and service fees into one number the operator cannot defend
leaving out-of-scope work undefined so it is absorbed silently
omitting the re-price triggers, so a growing client is served at a price set for a smaller one
acceptance_tests: every proposal shows the platform component and the operator's service component separately, with the service component traceable to a documented touch-time and complexity build
the scope statement lists inclusions, exclusions, late-input handling, out-of-scope charging and the named re-price triggers
revisit_triggers: actual touch time on serviced clients diverges from the build assumptions
the platform changes its pricing or packaging
a re-price trigger fires on an existing client without a defined response

base.update_signal: measured touch time on the serviced book departs from the pricing build, or the platform changes its pricing or packaging structure

nodes.definition: Close acquisition with a defined packet rather than an announcement, because the boundary between selling and onboarding is where the promises made in the sale either survive or evaporate. The packet is small and strictly bounded: the signed agreement or confirmed platform enrolment with the attribution mechanism recorded and evidenced; the complexity profile with its coarse score and the specific dimensions that drove it; the fit outcome with any conditional-fit limitations the prospect acknowledged in writing; the agreed target cutover boundary and the backward-planned dates the registration classes imply; the named client-side owner of the change and the named decision maker, which are frequently not the same person; the list of implicated registration and authorisation classes with held-or-needed markers; the commercial scope statement and price build; the referral source and any reporting-back commitments owed to them; and an explicit list of promises made during the sale, in the seller's own words, so onboarding inherits the expectations rather than discovering them. The gate is that acquisition does not hand over until each element is present and the conditional-fit limitations are acknowledged, because an unacknowledged limitation becomes an onboarding complaint. What the packet deliberately excludes is any of the onboarding work itself: no employee data, no balances, no setup steps, no migration plan - those begin on the other side of this line.

included: the contents of the handoff packet and the pass conditions of the gate
the explicit record of promises made during the sale
the exclusion of onboarding work and employee data from the packet
excluded: the onboarding project itself, including data migration, balance loading, account setup and parallel-run verification
the recurring service rhythm after go-live
any employee-level data, which is collected under onboarding controls rather than during acquisition

pros.claim: A written promise list stops the most common onboarding conflict, which is a client expecting something the seller said and nobody recorded
pros.example: an onboarding lead discovering in the packet that the client was told a particular report would be produced manually each period

pros.claim: Gating the handoff keeps unresolved acquisition work from being rediscovered as an implementation blocker
pros.example: a missing jurisdiction registration surfacing at the gate rather than three days before a planned cutover

cons.claim: The gate delays celebration and can hold up a start the client already believes has begun
cons.example: a signed client waiting while an unacknowledged limitation is put in writing and confirmed

cons.claim: Packet discipline is administrative overhead that a solo operator serving both sides of the boundary is tempted to skip
cons.example: an operator who sells and onboards the same client and believes the record is unnecessary because they remember everything

failure_modes: handing over verbally with no record of the promises made
leaving conditional-fit limitations unacknowledged by the client
omitting the referral source and the reporting-back commitments owed to them
including employee-level data in the packet because it was volunteered during the sale
acceptance_tests: the packet contains every listed element and the gate checklist is signed off before onboarding begins
the promises list is written in the seller's own words and the client has acknowledged each conditional-fit limitation in writing
revisit_triggers: an onboarding or early-service dispute traces to an expectation absent from the packet
the engagement rung changes what acquisition must hand over
a packet element is repeatedly missing at the gate

base.update_signal: onboarding or early-service disputes trace back to expectations the packet did not capture, or the engagement rung changes the handoff contents

qualify from aggregates and redacted extracts only
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: aggregate first, request a redacted extract only for a named unresolved dimension, transmit through a controlled channel, and delete on a stated schedule

conflict_axes.name: invoice_ownership_versus_liability_distance
conflict_axes.description: Owning the client's invoice creates margin control and a defensible book, and simultaneously imports receivable risk, price-increase defence and a support expectation on paydays.
poles: own the price and the client relationship
stay at introduction distance from execution risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose the rung by demonstrated support capacity and cash tolerance rather than by margin ambition, and re-test the choice whenever staffing changes

conflict_axes.name: single_platform_depth_versus_optionality
conflict_axes.description: Depth on one platform produces speed, fluency and tier progression; it also concentrates the practice's fate in one company's program decisions and capability gaps.
poles: go deep on one platform
hold a second relationship for profiles the first cannot serve
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stay single-platform while decline rates are low, and open a second relationship when declines concentrate in a profile class the niche keeps producing

conflict_axes.name: referral_source_covenant_versus_expansion_appetite
conflict_axes.description: The clients a bookkeeper or accountant hands over are the easiest place to sell adjacent work, and doing so ends the channel that produced them.
poles: expand into the adjacent work the client asks for
hold the do-not-solicit covenant
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the covenant wins by default; expansion requires the referring professional's written release, and the request is otherwise handed back to them

conflict_axes.name: niche_concentration_versus_pipeline_breadth
conflict_axes.description: Specialising compounds expertise and referral flow inside an industry while narrowing the addressable pipeline and correlating the book's risk.
poles: concentrate in one or two verticals
keep the pipeline open to any small employer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: concentrate where the platform's demonstrated capability covers the vertical's quirk set, and keep a general lane only for profiles the niche work already serves well

conflict_axes.name: helpful_answer_versus_scope_of_practice
conflict_axes.description: Small employers want one confident answer about their own tax and classification situation, and giving it is both the fastest way to be useful and the fastest way to create liability.
poles: answer the client's question directly
name the class and refer the instance out
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer class questions fully and refuse instance questions in writing with a referral, keeping the explanation generous and the determination someone else's

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_revenue_versus_diligence_depth
conflict_axes.description: Every week spent testing a platform's support path, reading the current agreement and building written arrangements is a week not spent placing clients.
poles: start placing clients now
finish diligence and written arrangements first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: time-box diligence and require only the disqualifier list and the attribution test before the first placement, deferring the rest to a scheduled completion date

edge_cases.description: A prospect is mid-quarter, has an agency notice in hand and an incumbent that has stopped responding, so the boundary rule and the client's exposure point in opposite directions
edge_cases.trigger: a live compliance failure appears far from any clean cutover boundary
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the notice as the client's own evidence, refer the notice response to a qualified professional, and justify a mid-period cutover in writing on the documented failure rather than on urgency created in the sale

edge_cases.description: A prospect states that everyone who works for them is a contractor and asks the operator to help keep it that way
edge_cases.trigger: the discovery conversation reveals a worker-classification signal
edge_cases.mitigation: name the class of question, refer to a qualified professional in writing, build no proposal on the disputed categorisation, and decline the account if the prospect wants a vendor to help them avoid a determination

edge_cases.description: A referring accountant is told by their professional body's rules that they may not accept the compensation the operator offered
edge_cases.trigger: verification of a regulated source's position returns a restriction after an arrangement was discussed
edge_cases.mitigation: withdraw the compensation offer immediately, restructure to a non-compensated referral relationship built on reciprocal value and reporting-back, and record the verification outcome in the relationship file

edge_cases.description: A prospect hires a remote employee in a jurisdiction where the business holds no accounts, three weeks before the agreed cutover
edge_cases.trigger: the work-location footprint changes after the profile was completed
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the implicated registration classes against the new footprint, re-plan the cutover backward from the registration lead time, and reset the client's date rather than compressing the work

edge_cases.description: A construction prospect needs certified or prevailing wage reporting that the platform cannot produce
edge_cases.trigger: a special regime in the profile falls outside demonstrated platform capability
edge_cases.mitigation: decline with the specific capability reason, point the prospect toward a product class that serves the regime where the operator can honestly do so, and record the decline so a repeated pattern triggers the second-platform question

edge_cases.description: A referred prospect turns out to have opened a self-serve account with the platform months earlier, so the partner attribution mechanism does not credit the introduction
edge_cases.trigger: an existing platform record pre-dates the operator's introduction
edge_cases.mitigation: check for a prior account before submitting the lead, raise the attribution question with the partner contact in writing before the prospect signs, and record the outcome whichever way it goes so the pattern is visible

edge_cases.description: The platform restructures its partner program while a pipeline of prospects was built on the previous compensation form
edge_cases.mitigation: read and date the new terms, re-model the practice on the new mechanism, re-check every promise made to referral sources under the old one, and correct any commitment that is no longer deliverable

edge_cases.description: A prospect offers the operator their current payroll system login so the operator can look at the setup themselves
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect volunteers credentials during discovery
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the credentials explicitly, explain why in a way that raises trust, and ask instead for the specific redacted extract that answers the open question

edge_cases.description: A placed client cancels early and the platform reverses compensation that the operator had already treated as earned
edge_cases.trigger: a cancellation falls inside the program's reversal exposure conditions
edge_cases.mitigation: treat compensation inside the exposure window as provisional in planning, review whether the cancellation traces to a fit judgement that should have been a decline, and feed the finding back into the match criteria

edge_cases.description: A prospect is visibly overwhelmed - a recent bereavement, a business crisis, or plain exhaustion - and is ready to sign anything put in front of them
edge_cases.trigger: distress or incapacity signals appear during the sales conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the process deliberately, put the summary and the recommendation in writing, encourage the prospect to involve an adviser or family member they trust, and decline a same-day commitment even when it is offered

edge_cases.description: A restaurant prospect runs tip pooling and a service charge arrangement whose payroll treatment the operator has not encountered
edge_cases.trigger: a vertical quirk appears that is outside the operator's tested niche knowledge
edge_cases.mitigation: say plainly that the arrangement needs to be confirmed before any commitment, test the platform's handling against the described arrangement, and route the treatment question to the client's own professional rather than improvising an answer

edge_cases.description: A referred client asks the operator to take over the bookkeeping that the referring firm currently performs
edge_cases.trigger: a serviced client invites expansion into the referrer's own service line
edge_cases.mitigation: decline and hand the request back to the referring firm, document the decline, and treat any exception as requiring the referrer's written release before it is even discussed with the client

workflow.action: Choose the engagement rung and write down what each party owns
workflow.description: Apply the capability, liability-coverage and cash tests to select introduce-only, wholesale reseller, or service bureau, and state what the operator, the platform and the client each own on that rung
workflow.gate: the rung is named, the payday-emergency owner is identified, and the professional liability coverage question has been put to an insurer

workflow.action: Fix the scope-of-practice and data-handling boundaries before any prospect contact
workflow.description: Write the class-versus-instance rule with worked examples, the refusal-and-referral script, the responsible-party statement, and the aggregate-first data rule with its retention schedule
workflow.gate: the rulebook contains a worked example on each side of the advice line and a written retention and deletion rule for pre-sale documents

workflow.action: Run time-boxed diligence on the platform and its partner program
workflow.description: Test the support path, read and date the current agreement, check console capability, ask existing partners about a bad period, and record concentration and termination answers against a pre-written disqualifier list
workflow.artifact: dated platform diligence file with disqualifier list
workflow.gate: every disqualifier item is marked met, not met, or unresolved, and no unresolved item blocks the first placement

workflow.action: Model the compensation mechanism rather than a number
workflow.description: Identify which payment forms apply on the chosen rung, name the drivers that move each, and record a dated extract of the terms in force
workflow.artifact: compensation mechanism model with component bands and dated terms extract
workflow.gate: no figure in the model lacks a trace to a dated program document or the operator's own price sheet

workflow.action: Stand up and test the attribution ledger before any lead is sent
workflow.description: Confirm the program's attribution mechanism, test it end to end, create the per-prospect ledger fields, and record the reversal exposure conditions currently in force
workflow.artifact: attribution ledger with a completed end-to-end test record
workflow.gate: an attribution test has been confirmed by the platform or by a controlled signup, and the ledger fields exist before the first introduction

workflow.action: Map the referral channel portfolio and pick the deep relationships
workflow.description: List the source classes, the motive assumed for each, the named relationships being worked, and the concentration limit that prevents single-source dependence
workflow.artifact: channel map with named relationships and concentration limit
workflow.gate: each class has a stated motive and at least one named relationship or a decision not to work it, and the concentration limit is written down

workflow.action: Verify restrictions and put referral arrangements in writing
workflow.description: For each compensated source, name the restriction class, obtain their recorded confirmation that they have checked their own position, and fix trigger, timing, reversal handling, disclosure, solicitation limits, termination and confidentiality in writing
workflow.artifact: signed referral arrangements with dated verification records
workflow.gate: no introduction is accepted from a compensated source without a dated verification record and a written arrangement

workflow.action: Run structured discovery on a triggered prospect
workflow.description: Work the situation-evidence-consequence-timing sequence, use the prospect's own documents as evidence, apply the restraint and vulnerable-operator rules, and write the summary back to the prospect
workflow.gate: the summary names the observed trigger with its evidence, the decision maker, and the timing constraint, and contains no employee-level identifiers or credentials

workflow.action: Complete and score the complexity profile
workflow.description: Capture worker counts, actual work jurisdictions, pay frequency and composition, deduction classes, special regimes, connected systems and growth plan in aggregate form, then score complexity coarsely
workflow.artifact: scored complexity profile with implicated registration classes listed
workflow.gate: every dimension is answered, the score names the dimension that drove it, and each implicated registration class carries a held-or-needed marker

workflow.action: Decide fit, conditional fit, or decline against demonstrated capability
workflow.description: Compare the profile dimension by dimension against evidence of what the platform has actually done, disclose the compensation relationship, and communicate the outcome including an honest direction on a decline
workflow.artifact: fit decision record with per-dimension evidence and outcome
workflow.gate: the compensation disclosure has been delivered, and any conditional-fit limitation is written and acknowledged by the prospect before a proposal is issued

workflow.action: Build the two-part offer and the price from the operator's own economics
workflow.description: Separate the platform component from the service layer, build the service price from touch time and complexity, and write the scope statement with exclusions, late-input handling and re-price triggers
workflow.artifact: proposal with separated components, touch-time price build and scope statement
workflow.gate: the service price traces to a documented touch-time build and the scope statement names its exclusions and re-price triggers

workflow.action: Assemble the handoff packet and pass the acquisition gate
workflow.description: Collect the enrolment and attribution evidence, profile and score, fit outcome and acknowledged limitations, target boundary and backward-planned dates, named client-side owner, registration class markers, scope and price, referral source obligations, and the promises list in the seller's own words
workflow.gate: every packet element is present, no employee-level data is included, and the conditional-fit limitations are acknowledged in writing before onboarding begins

dominance_rules.rule: Client data confidentiality and least-privilege handling dominate every sales convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: payroll data is the densest concentration of harmful information a small employer holds, and an acquisition-stage leak destroys both the deal and the referral channel that produced it
dominance_rules.trigger: any request, offer, or shortcut that would put employee identifiers, wage detail, bank details or credentials into the operator's hands before they are needed
dominance_rules.action: refuse the data or the credentials, ask instead for the aggregate or redacted extract that answers the specific open question, and record the refusal

dominance_rules.rationale: payroll sits in a compliance-critical professional domain where a confident wrong answer produces assessed penalties for the client and liability for the operator
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect asks for a determination about their own tax position, worker classification, or agency notice
dominance_rules.action: answer the class question, refuse the instance question, and refer to a qualified professional in the client's jurisdiction in writing before the conversation moves on

dominance_rules.rule: Fit dominates compensation in every recommendation
dominance_rules.rationale: a payroll misfit is a recurring operational failure that surfaces every pay period and lands on the client's employees, while a lost placement costs the operator only one deal
dominance_rules.trigger: the option that fits the client's profile differs from the option that pays the operator more
dominance_rules.action: recommend the fitting option or decline the deal, and never let a compensation difference break a tie on a capability question

dominance_rules.rationale: a prospect can only weigh a compensated recommendation if they know it is one, and learning it later from a third party destroys the relationship
dominance_rules.trigger: the operator is about to name a platform or make a recommendation
dominance_rules.action: state the partner relationship and the form of compensation aloud first, and mirror it in the written proposal

dominance_rules.rule: A documented live failure dominates the boundary calendar; otherwise the calendar dominates close-now pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: boundary cutovers remove an entire class of migration risk, but waiting while exposure accrues costs the client more than the migration would
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect wants to move mid-period, or the operator wants to close mid-period
dominance_rules.action: require a written justification naming the live failure to break the calendar, and otherwise park the deal with a scheduled return date

dominance_rules.rationale: a distressed owner signing something they do not understand is the worst outcome available in this business and is not repaired by a good implementation
dominance_rules.trigger: distress, incapacity, exhaustion, or crisis signals appear in the sales conversation
dominance_rules.action: slow down, put the recommendation in writing, encourage involvement of someone the prospect trusts, and decline a same-day commitment

dominance_rules.rule: Written and dated program terms dominate any verbal assurance from a platform representative
dominance_rules.rationale: partner programs are revised unilaterally and representatives change, so memory and goodwill are not evidence when compensation or attribution is disputed
dominance_rules.trigger: a compensation, attribution, or capability question arises during a deal
dominance_rules.action: read the current terms, record a dated extract, and quote nothing that cannot be traced to it

dominance_rules.rule: The referral source covenant dominates expansion appetite
dominance_rules.rationale: the accounting relationship that produces steady introductions is worth more than any single adjacent engagement, and word travels fast inside a professional community
dominance_rules.trigger: a referred client asks the operator to take on work belonging to the referring professional
dominance_rules.action: decline, hand the request back to the referrer, and proceed only on the referrer's written release

dominance_rules.rule: Verification of a regulated source's own position dominates a promised share
dominance_rules.rationale: the operator cannot bind another professional's compliance obligations, and an impermissible payment harms the source far more than it helps the operator
dominance_rules.trigger: a compensated referral arrangement is proposed to a licensed or regulated source
dominance_rules.action: obtain and date their confirmation that they have checked their own position before any introduction, and restructure to a non-compensated relationship if the answer is restrictive

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence of demonstrated capability dominates capability claims when judging fit
dominance_rules.rationale: salespeople describe roadmaps and edge cases optimistically, and the cost of the error is borne every pay period by the client
dominance_rules.trigger: a profile dimension depends on a capability the operator has not seen working
dominance_rules.action: treat the dimension as unproven, seek a demonstration or a partner reference, and record the outcome as a conditional fit with a written limitation if it cannot be proven

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete platform and program diligence, including the error-and-penalty posture and the termination-of-book clause, before recruiting a single referral source
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to explain a platform weakness to professionals who have already staked their own reputation on the operator's recommendation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set up and test the attribution mechanism before sending the first prospect
anti_rework_rules.prevents: working an entire early pipeline for compensation that is never credited and cannot be reconstructed afterwards

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a regulated source's own compensation restrictions before proposing any share
anti_rework_rules.prevents: withdrawing an offer already made, and the relationship damage of having put a professional in an impermissible position

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the complexity profile before quoting a price or naming a go-live date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repricing and re-timing an engagement after a special regime, extra jurisdiction or unusual pay type surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm where employees actually work and which registration classes are held before recommending a platform or a boundary
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at cutover that a missing employer account or third-party authorisation makes the promised date impossible

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask about the incumbent's contract terms, notice period and data export before agreeing a cutover date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cutover plan built around a date the client cannot actually leave on, and a scramble for records the outgoing provider controls

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the disclosure wording and the do-not-solicit covenant before the first joint meeting with a referral source's client
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an improvised answer in front of the referrer that has to be walked back and rebuilt into trust later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate a candidate vertical against demonstrated platform capability before building any niche positioning or collateral
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an acquisition engine that reliably produces prospects the operator must decline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write down every promise made during the sale, in the seller's own words, before the handoff gate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: onboarding discovering commitments it cannot meet and a client relationship that starts with a correction

iteration_protocol.trigger: the platform revises partner program terms, compensation form, or attribution mechanism
iteration_protocol.action: re-read and date the new terms, re-model the compensation mechanism, re-test attribution end to end, and review every promise made to referral sources under the previous terms

iteration_protocol.trigger: an expected credit fails to arrive or is reversed
iteration_protocol.action: reconstruct the ledger entry, raise it with the platform contact in writing, and repair the attribution step that failed before more introductions are sent

iteration_protocol.trigger: declines concentrate in one profile class that the niche keeps producing
iteration_protocol.action: review whether the niche or the platform is the mismatch, and decide deliberately between narrowing the niche and opening a second platform relationship

iteration_protocol.trigger: a placed client leaves early or an onboarding dispute traces to an expectation nobody recorded
iteration_protocol.action: trace the failure back to the discovery question, fit judgement or promise that produced it, and amend the intake, match criteria or packet accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: opportunities repeatedly stall at the boundary and parked deals decay
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the backward plan from registration lead times, tighten the nurture cadence for parked prospects, and re-brief referral sources on the signals that indicate a trigger

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prospect, client, or referral source describes the sales conversation as pressuring, or new collateral enters the process
iteration_protocol.action: audit call notes and material for penalty figures, audit-probability claims and urgency framings, correct them, and re-rehearse the class-level register and the vulnerable-operator rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new jurisdiction, special regime, or pay type appears repeatedly in the pipeline
iteration_protocol.action: add the dimension to the intake form, re-check the implicated registration classes, and test the platform's handling before it is promised to anyone

iteration_protocol.trigger: the serviced book, staffing, or engagement rung changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-test the rung against the coverage and cash tests, re-derive the service price from measured touch time, and update what the operator promises referral sources

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the engagement rung, the advice boundary, the data-handling rule and the disclosure habit determine what the operator may say, collect and promise in every later step; the model and economics nodes follow because compensation and attribution mechanics decide whether any of the work is actually paid; platform diligence and the client profile then supply the two evidence bases that the honest fit decision compares; channel and niche nodes build the flow of prospects that the trigger map and boundary calendar convert into correctly timed opportunities; and discovery, risk-talk discipline, the two-part offer and the handoff packet come last because they compose everything above into a single qualified, honestly timed deal that onboarding can inherit without rework.
